paragraphs.en: Every Sunday morning, I go to the park near my house. The air is fresh, and the birds sing in the trees. Many people are already there when I arrive.
paragraphs.zh: 每個星期天早上，我都會去家附近的公園。空氣很清新，鳥兒在樹上唱歌。當我到達時，已經有許多人在那裡了。

paragraphs.en: Some old people do exercise together under a big tree. Children run and laugh on the grass. A young man plays the guitar and sings songs.
paragraphs.zh: 一些老人家在大樹下一起做運動。孩子們在草地上奔跑歡笑。一位年輕人彈著吉他唱歌。

paragraphs.en: I like to sit on a bench and read a book. Sometimes I just watch the people and smile. A simple morning in the park always makes me happy.
paragraphs.zh: 我喜歡坐在長椅上看書。有時候我只是看著人們，微笑著。公園裡簡單的早晨總是讓我很快樂。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I took my first cooking class. Our teacher was a friendly woman with twenty years of experience. She taught us how to make a simple pasta dish.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我上了第一堂烹飪課。我們的老師是一位友善的女士，有二十年的經驗。她教我們做一道簡單的義大利麵。

paragraphs.en: At first, I was nervous. I cut the vegetables too big, and I put too much salt in the sauce. The teacher smiled and said, "Don't worry. Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning."
paragraphs.zh: 起初我很緊張。我把蔬菜切得太大塊，醬汁裡放了太多鹽。老師微笑著說：「別擔心，每個人剛開始都會犯錯。」

paragraphs.en: After two hours, my pasta was ready. It was not perfect, but it tasted good. Now I cook dinner for my family every weekend. Cooking is my new hobby.
paragraphs.zh: 兩個小時後，我的義大利麵完成了。雖然不完美，但味道很好。現在我每個週末都為家人做晚餐。烹飪成了我的新嗜好。

paragraphs.en: One rainy evening, I found a small cat outside my door. It was wet and cold, and it looked very hungry. I gave it some food and a warm towel.
paragraphs.zh: 一個下雨的傍晚，我在門外發現一隻小貓。牠又濕又冷，看起來非常餓。我給了牠一些食物和一條溫暖的毛巾。

paragraphs.en: The next day, I made posters with the cat's picture. I put them around my neighborhood. Three days later, a little girl called me. She was crying with joy.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，我做了印有貓咪照片的海報，貼在住家附近。三天後，一個小女孩打電話給我。她高興得哭了。

paragraphs.en: The cat's name was Coco, and it was her best friend. When they met again, Coco jumped into her arms. Helping them find each other was a wonderful feeling.
paragraphs.zh: 那隻貓的名字叫可可，是她最好的朋友。當他們再次見面時，可可跳進了她的懷裡。幫助他們重逢的感覺真美好。

title: ★ A Trip to the Night Market

paragraphs.en: Taiwan is famous for its night markets. Last Friday, my foreign friend David visited me, and I took him to the biggest night market in the city.
paragraphs.zh: 台灣以夜市聞名。上週五，我的外國朋友大衛來找我，我帶他去市區最大的夜市。

paragraphs.en: David tried many kinds of food. He loved the fried chicken and the bubble tea. He was afraid of the stinky tofu at first, but after one bite, he asked for more!
paragraphs.zh: 大衛嘗試了很多種食物。他很喜歡炸雞和珍珠奶茶。他一開始不敢吃臭豆腐，但咬了一口之後，竟然還想再吃！

paragraphs.en: We also played games and won a small toy. David said it was the best night of his trip. Food, games, and friends - a night market has everything.
paragraphs.zh: 我們還玩了遊戲，贏得一個小玩具。大衛說這是他旅程中最棒的一晚。美食、遊戲和朋友——夜市什麼都有。

paragraphs.en: My daughter is six years old. Last week, she asked me to teach her how to ride a bicycle. We went to the school playground on Saturday morning.
paragraphs.zh: 我的女兒六歲了。上週，她請我教她騎腳踏車。星期六早上，我們去了學校的操場。

paragraphs.en: She fell down many times, but she did not cry. She stood up, smiled, and tried again. After two hours, she could ride slowly without my help.
paragraphs.zh: 她跌倒了很多次，但沒有哭。她站起來，微笑著再試一次。兩個小時後，她已經可以不用我扶，慢慢地騎了。

paragraphs.en: When she rode across the playground alone, she shouted, "Daddy, look at me!" I felt so proud. Children teach us that we should never give up.
paragraphs.zh: 當她獨自騎過操場時，她大喊：「爸爸，你看我！」我感到非常驕傲。孩子們教會我們永遠不要放棄。

paragraphs.en: Each season has its own beauty. In spring, flowers open and the world turns green. The weather is warm, and people like to walk outside.
paragraphs.zh: 每個季節都有自己的美。春天，花朵綻放，世界變成一片綠意。天氣溫暖，人們喜歡外出散步。

paragraphs.en: Summer brings hot days and bright sunshine. Families go to the beach and children swim in the sea. In autumn, the leaves turn red and yellow, and the air becomes cool.
paragraphs.zh: 夏天帶來炎熱的日子和明亮的陽光。全家人去海邊，孩子們在海裡游泳。秋天，樹葉轉紅變黃，空氣變得涼爽。

paragraphs.en: Winter is quiet and cold. In some places, snow covers the ground like a white blanket. People drink hot tea and stay warm at home. Which season do you like best?
paragraphs.zh: 冬天安靜而寒冷。在某些地方，白雪像一條白毯子覆蓋大地。人們喝著熱茶，待在溫暖的家裡。你最喜歡哪個季節呢？

title: ★ A Letter to My Future Self

paragraphs.en: Dear future me, how are you? Today I am fifteen years old, and I am writing this letter in my English class. I want to ask you some questions.
paragraphs.zh: 親愛的未來的我，你好嗎？今天我十五歲，正在英文課上寫這封信。我想問你幾個問題。

paragraphs.en: Did you become a doctor like you dreamed? Do you still play basketball with your old friends? I hope you take care of Mom and Dad, and I hope you are happy.
paragraphs.zh: 你有沒有像夢想的那樣成為醫生？你還和老朋友們打籃球嗎？我希望你好好照顧爸爸媽媽，也希望你過得快樂。

paragraphs.en: Right now, I study hard every day. Sometimes it is difficult, but I will not stop. Future me, please remember: you were a brave kid with a big dream.
paragraphs.zh: 現在，我每天都努力讀書。有時候很辛苦，但我不會停下來。未來的我，請記住：你曾是一個懷抱大夢想的勇敢孩子。

paragraphs.en: Many people believe that sleeping less means achieving more. However, science tells a different story. Sleep is not wasted time; it is when our body repairs itself and our brain organizes memories.
paragraphs.zh: 許多人認為睡得少代表能完成更多事。然而，科學告訴我們並非如此。睡眠不是浪費時間；那是身體自我修復、大腦整理記憶的時刻。

paragraphs.en: Research shows that adults need seven to nine hours of sleep each night. People who sleep less than six hours have a higher risk of heart disease, weight gain, and depression. Lack of sleep also weakens our ability to focus and make decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 研究顯示，成年人每晚需要七到九小時的睡眠。睡不到六小時的人，罹患心臟病、體重增加和憂鬱症的風險較高。睡眠不足也會削弱我們專注和做決定的能力。

paragraphs.en: To sleep better, experts suggest keeping a regular schedule, avoiding screens before bedtime, and keeping the bedroom dark and quiet. Good sleep is not a luxury - it is a necessary part of a healthy life.
paragraphs.zh: 想要睡得更好，專家建議維持規律的作息、睡前避免使用螢幕，並保持臥室黑暗安靜。良好的睡眠不是奢侈品——而是健康生活不可或缺的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Most people fail to change their lives because they aim too high too quickly. They promise to exercise for an hour every day or to read fifty books a year. After two weeks, they give up and feel disappointed.
paragraphs.zh: 大多數人無法改變生活，是因為一開始就把目標訂得太高。他們承諾每天運動一小時，或一年讀五十本書。兩週之後就放棄了，並感到失望。

paragraphs.en: A better approach is to start with tiny habits. Instead of an hour of exercise, do five minutes. Instead of a whole book, read one page before bed. Small actions are easy to repeat, and repetition is what creates real change.
paragraphs.zh: 更好的方法是從微小的習慣開始。與其運動一小時，不如先做五分鐘。與其讀完一整本書，不如睡前讀一頁。小行動容易重複，而重複正是創造真正改變的關鍵。

paragraphs.en: Over time, these small habits grow naturally. Five minutes becomes twenty, and one page becomes one chapter. As the writer James Clear says, you do not rise to the level of your goals; you fall to the level of your systems.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著時間過去，這些小習慣會自然成長。五分鐘變成二十分鐘，一頁變成一章。正如作家詹姆斯・克利爾所說：你不會達到目標的高度，而是會落到系統的水準。

paragraphs.en: Coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world, but people enjoy it in very different ways. In Italy, people stand at a bar and finish a small espresso in two minutes. Ordering a large milky coffee after lunch is considered strange.
paragraphs.zh: 咖啡是世界上最受歡迎的飲品之一，但各地的人享用方式大不相同。在義大利，人們站在吧台前，兩分鐘內喝完一小杯濃縮咖啡。午餐後點一大杯加奶咖啡會被認為很奇怪。

paragraphs.en: In Turkey, coffee is cooked slowly in a small pot and served with sweets. It is so important to the culture that UNESCO added Turkish coffee to its cultural heritage list. In Sweden, people enjoy 'fika' - a daily coffee break with friends that is almost a national tradition.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其，咖啡用小壺慢慢煮，並搭配甜點享用。它對文化如此重要，聯合國教科文組織甚至將土耳其咖啡列入文化遺產名錄。在瑞典，人們享受「fika」——每天與朋友的咖啡時光，幾乎是一種全民傳統。

paragraphs.en: Whether it is a quick shot in Rome or a slow afternoon in Stockholm, coffee does the same job everywhere: it brings people together. The next time you travel, try drinking coffee the local way.
paragraphs.zh: 無論是在羅馬快速喝一杯，還是在斯德哥爾摩度過緩慢的午後，咖啡在世界各地的作用都一樣：把人們聚在一起。下次旅行時，不妨試著用當地的方式喝咖啡。

title: ★ Should Students Use AI for Homework?
title_zh: 學生應該用 AI 寫作業嗎？

paragraphs.en: Artificial intelligence tools can now write essays, solve math problems, and answer almost any question. This creates a difficult question for schools: should students be allowed to use AI for their homework?
paragraphs.zh: 人工智慧工具現在可以寫文章、解數學題，回答幾乎任何問題。這為學校帶來一個難題：應該允許學生用 AI 寫作業嗎？

paragraphs.en: Some teachers worry that students will stop thinking for themselves. If AI writes your essay, you learn nothing about writing. Others argue that AI is like a calculator - a tool that everyone will use at work, so students should learn to use it well.
paragraphs.zh: 有些老師擔心學生會停止自己思考。如果 AI 幫你寫文章，你就學不到任何寫作能力。另一些人則認為 AI 就像計算機——是每個人工作時都會用到的工具，所以學生應該學會善用它。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the answer lies in the middle. Students can use AI to check grammar, get ideas, or understand difficult concepts, but the final thinking should be their own. The goal of education is not to produce perfect homework - it is to produce thinking people.
paragraphs.zh: 也許答案就在中間。學生可以用 AI 檢查文法、獲得靈感或理解困難的概念，但最終的思考應該是自己的。教育的目的不是產出完美的作業——而是培養會思考的人。

paragraphs.en: A honeybee colony is one of nature's most amazing societies. Up to 60,000 bees live together in a single hive, and each bee has a clear job. Workers collect food, guards protect the entrance, and the queen lays all the eggs.
paragraphs.zh: 蜂群是大自然最令人驚嘆的社會之一。多達六萬隻蜜蜂共同生活在一個蜂巢裡，每隻蜜蜂都有明確的工作。工蜂採集食物，守衛蜂保護入口，蜂后則負責產下所有的卵。

paragraphs.en: Bees even have their own language. When a worker finds flowers full of nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a special dance. The direction and speed of her dance tell other bees exactly where to find the food.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂甚至有自己的語言。當工蜂發現滿是花蜜的花朵時，她會回到蜂巢跳一種特別的舞。舞蹈的方向和速度能準確告訴其他蜜蜂食物的位置。

paragraphs.en: Bees matter far beyond honey. About one third of the food we eat depends on their pollination. Protecting bees means protecting our own dinner table - a fact worth remembering the next time one buzzes past you.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂的重要性遠不止於蜂蜜。我們吃的食物約有三分之一仰賴牠們授粉。保護蜜蜂就是保護我們自己的餐桌——下次有蜜蜂從你身邊嗡嗡飛過時，值得記住這一點。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I tried an experiment: I turned off my phone for an entire weekend. The first few hours were uncomfortable. My hand kept reaching for my pocket, and I felt strangely anxious, as if I were missing something important.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我做了一個實驗：整個週末關掉手機。最初幾個小時很不自在。我的手不斷伸向口袋，我感到莫名的焦慮，彷彿錯過了什麼重要的事。

paragraphs.en: By Saturday afternoon, something changed. I finished a novel I had started months ago. I cooked a proper meal instead of ordering delivery. In the evening, I had a three-hour conversation with my parents - without checking notifications once.
paragraphs.zh: 到了星期六下午，情況開始改變。我讀完了幾個月前開始看的小說。我好好煮了一頓飯，而不是叫外送。晚上，我和父母聊了三個小時——一次都沒有查看通知。

paragraphs.en: On Monday, I turned my phone back on. I had 47 messages, but honestly, none of them were urgent. The world had continued perfectly well without my attention. Now I take a phone-free evening every week, and I protect it like an important meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 星期一，我重新開機。有四十七則訊息，但說實話，沒有一則是緊急的。沒有我的關注，世界依然運轉得很好。現在我每週都安排一個不用手機的晚上，並像重要會議一樣守護這段時間。

title: ★ How the Bullet Train Got Its Nose

paragraphs.en: Japan's bullet trains are famous for their speed, but early models had a serious problem. Every time a train exited a tunnel at high speed, it produced a loud boom that disturbed residents living nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 日本的子彈列車以速度聞名，但早期的車型有個嚴重的問題。每當列車高速駛出隧道時，都會產生巨大的聲響，干擾附近的居民。

paragraphs.en: An engineer named Eiji Nakatsu found the answer in nature. He was a birdwatcher, and he noticed that the kingfisher dives into water at high speed with almost no splash. Its long, narrow beak cuts smoothly through the change between air and water.
paragraphs.zh: 一位名叫中津英治的工程師在大自然中找到了答案。他是一位賞鳥愛好者，注意到翠鳥高速衝入水中時幾乎不會濺起水花。牠細長的鳥喙能順暢地穿過空氣與水之間的交界。

paragraphs.en: The team redesigned the train's front to copy the kingfisher's beak. The new train was not only quieter - it also used 15 percent less electricity and ran 10 percent faster. Nature had already solved the problem millions of years ago; engineers just needed to look.
paragraphs.zh: 團隊模仿翠鳥的喙重新設計了車頭。新列車不僅更安靜，還省了百分之十五的電力，速度快了百分之十。大自然早在數百萬年前就解決了這個問題；工程師只需要用心觀察。

paragraphs.en: Streaming has fundamentally transformed the music industry. Two decades ago, artists earned revenue primarily through album sales; today, the vast majority of listening happens on platforms that pay fractions of a cent per stream.
paragraphs.zh: 串流媒體徹底改變了音樂產業。二十年前，歌手主要靠專輯銷售賺取收入；如今，絕大多數的聆聽都發生在每次播放僅支付不到一美分的平台上。

paragraphs.en: This shift has produced winners and losers. Global superstars with billions of streams accumulate substantial income, while independent musicians often receive monthly payments that barely cover a meal. Consequently, many artists now rely on touring, merchandise, and brand partnerships as their primary sources of revenue.
paragraphs.zh: 這種轉變造就了贏家與輸家。擁有數十億次播放量的全球巨星累積了可觀的收入，而獨立音樂人每月拿到的錢往往連一頓飯都不夠。因此，許多歌手現在把巡演、周邊商品和品牌合作當作主要收入來源。

paragraphs.en: Critics argue the system is unsustainable, yet streaming has also democratized access: any musician can now reach a global audience without a record label. The question facing the industry is not whether streaming will survive, but whether a fairer distribution model can emerge from it.
paragraphs.zh: 批評者認為這種制度難以持續，但串流也讓機會變得更平等：任何音樂人現在都能不靠唱片公司接觸全球聽眾。產業面臨的問題不是串流能否存活，而是能否從中發展出更公平的分配模式。

paragraphs.en: Cities are consistently warmer than the countryside around them, a phenomenon scientists call the urban heat island effect. Concrete and asphalt absorb solar radiation during the day and release it slowly at night, keeping temperatures elevated around the clock.
paragraphs.zh: 城市總是比周圍的鄉村更溫暖，科學家稱這種現象為都市熱島效應。混凝土和柏油在白天吸收太陽輻射，夜間再緩慢釋放，使氣溫全天維持在較高的水準。

paragraphs.en: The consequences extend beyond discomfort. Higher temperatures increase electricity demand for air conditioning, worsen air pollution, and pose genuine health risks to elderly residents. During heat waves, urban neighborhoods with few trees record significantly more hospital admissions than greener districts.
paragraphs.zh: 其後果不僅止於不舒適。更高的氣溫增加了空調用電需求、惡化空氣污染，並對年長居民構成實際的健康風險。熱浪期間，樹木稀少的市區社區就醫人數明顯高於綠化較多的地區。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, solutions exist and are relatively affordable. Planting street trees, painting rooftops white, and preserving urban parks can lower local temperatures by several degrees. The challenge is not technical but political: cities must prioritize long-term livability over short-term development profits.
paragraphs.zh: 幸運的是，解決方案是存在的，而且成本相對低廉。種植行道樹、將屋頂漆成白色、保留城市公園，都能讓局部氣溫降低好幾度。挑戰不在技術，而在政治：城市必須把長期宜居性置於短期開發利益之上。

paragraphs.en: Procrastination is commonly misunderstood as laziness or poor time management. Psychological research suggests otherwise: procrastination is primarily an emotional regulation problem. We delay tasks not because we cannot schedule them, but because they trigger negative feelings - boredom, anxiety, or self-doubt.
paragraphs.zh: 拖延常被誤解為懶惰或不會管理時間。心理學研究卻指出並非如此：拖延主要是情緒調節的問題。我們延遲任務，不是因為排不出時間，而是因為這些任務引發了負面情緒——無聊、焦慮或自我懷疑。

paragraphs.en: When we avoid a difficult task, we feel immediate relief, and the brain registers this relief as a reward. This creates a vicious cycle: each avoidance strengthens the habit, while the postponed task grows more intimidating. Paradoxically, people often procrastinate most on the goals they care about most deeply.
paragraphs.zh: 當我們逃避困難的任務時，會立刻感到輕鬆，而大腦會把這種輕鬆記錄為一種獎勵。這形成了惡性循環：每一次逃避都強化了這個習慣，而被延後的任務則變得越來越可怕。矛盾的是，人們最常拖延的，往往是自己最在乎的目標。

paragraphs.en: Effective remedies therefore target emotions rather than calendars. Breaking work into trivially small steps reduces the fear of starting; practicing self-compassion after setbacks prevents the shame spiral that fuels further delay. The counterintuitive lesson is that forgiving yourself for procrastinating is one of the most effective ways to stop doing it.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，有效的解方針對的是情緒，而不是行事曆。把工作拆成極小的步驟能降低開始的恐懼；在挫折後練習自我疼惜，能避免助長進一步拖延的羞愧漩渦。反直覺的啟示是：原諒自己的拖延，正是停止拖延最有效的方法之一。

title: ★ What Octopuses Teach Us About Intelligence

paragraphs.en: The octopus presents a fascinating puzzle for scientists studying intelligence. Its last common ancestor with humans was a simple worm that lived 600 million years ago, yet octopuses solve mazes, open jars, use tools, and appear to play - abilities we normally associate with mammals and birds.
paragraphs.zh: 對研究智慧的科學家而言，章魚是個迷人的謎題。牠與人類最近的共同祖先是六億年前的一種簡單蠕蟲，然而章魚會走迷宮、開罐子、使用工具，甚至似乎會玩耍——這些能力我們通常只與哺乳類和鳥類聯想在一起。

paragraphs.en: Their intelligence is organized in a radically different way. Two thirds of an octopus's neurons reside not in its brain but in its arms, which can taste, touch, and make decisions semi-independently. In a sense, each arm has a mind of its own, and the central brain acts more like a coordinator than a commander.
paragraphs.zh: 牠們的智慧以截然不同的方式組織。章魚三分之二的神經元不在大腦，而在牠的腕足裡；這些腕足能嚐味道、有觸覺，並且能半獨立地做決定。某種意義上，每條腕足都有自己的心智，而中央大腦更像協調者，而非指揮官。

paragraphs.en: This matters because octopuses demonstrate that intelligence is not a single ladder with humans at the top, but a landscape with multiple peaks. Evolution invented minds at least twice, through entirely different architectures. If we ever encounter intelligence beyond Earth, the octopus reminds us it may look nothing like our own.
paragraphs.zh: 這件事之所以重要，是因為章魚證明了智慧不是一座以人類為頂端的階梯，而是一片擁有多座山峰的地景。演化至少用完全不同的架構「發明」了兩次心智。如果有一天我們遇到地球以外的智慧，章魚提醒我們：它可能與我們的智慧毫無相似之處。

title: ★ The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion

paragraphs.en: Fast fashion has made clothing astonishingly cheap and abundant. A t-shirt costs less than a sandwich, and new styles arrive in stores every week. Yet this convenience conceals substantial costs that never appear on the price tag.
paragraphs.zh: 快時尚讓衣服變得驚人地便宜且大量。一件 T 恤比一份三明治還便宜，而且新款式每週都會上架。然而，這種便利掩蓋了從未出現在價格標籤上的龐大代價。

paragraphs.en: The environmental burden is severe: the fashion industry consumes enormous quantities of water, and produces roughly ten percent of global carbon emissions - more than international flights and shipping combined. Meanwhile, the majority of discarded clothing ends up in landfills, often in developing countries that never asked to receive it.
paragraphs.zh: 環境負擔十分沉重：時尚產業消耗大量的水，並產生全球約百分之十的碳排放——比國際航空和海運加起來還多。同時，大多數被丟棄的衣物最終進了垃圾掩埋場，而且往往落在從未要求接收它們的開發中國家。

paragraphs.en: Consumers are not powerless, however. Buying fewer, higher-quality garments, choosing second-hand clothing, and simply wearing clothes longer can significantly reduce this impact. Research suggests that extending a garment's life by just nine months reduces its environmental footprint by twenty to thirty percent. The most sustainable shirt, it turns out, is the one already in your closet.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，消費者並非無能為力。少買一些、選擇品質更好的衣物、購買二手衣，或單純把衣服穿久一點，都能顯著減少這種影響。研究指出，只要將一件衣服的壽命延長九個月，就能減少百分之二十到三十的環境足跡。事實證明，最環保的襯衫，就是你衣櫃裡已經有的那一件。

title: ★ Remote Work and the Future of Cities
title_zh: 遠距工作與城市的未來

paragraphs.en: The pandemic proved that millions of jobs can be performed from anywhere with a laptop and a stable connection. Years later, the consequences are still reshaping urban economies in ways few predicted.
paragraphs.zh: 疫情證明了數百萬份工作只要有筆電和穩定的網路，在任何地方都能完成。多年後，其後果仍在以少有人預料到的方式重塑城市經濟。

paragraphs.en: Downtown districts built around office workers have suffered the most. Coffee shops, dry cleaners, and lunch restaurants lost their weekday customers, and some office towers report vacancy rates above thirty percent. Meanwhile, smaller towns and suburbs have experienced an influx of remote professionals seeking space and affordability, driving up housing prices far from traditional job centers.
paragraphs.zh: 圍繞上班族打造的市中心區受創最深。咖啡店、乾洗店和午餐餐廳失去了平日的顧客，一些辦公大樓的空置率超過百分之三十。與此同時，較小的城鎮和郊區湧入了尋求空間與可負擔生活的遠距工作者，推高了遠離傳統就業中心地區的房價。

paragraphs.en: Cities now face a choice: adapt or decline. Some are converting empty offices into apartments; others are redesigning downtowns around culture and entertainment rather than commuting. The office is not dead, but its monopoly on work has ended - and the cities that thrive will be those that give people reasons beyond employment to gather.
paragraphs.zh: 城市現在面臨抉擇：轉型或衰退。有些城市正把空辦公室改建成住宅；有些則圍繞文化和娛樂而非通勤重新設計市中心。辦公室並未消亡，但它對工作的壟斷已經結束——能夠繁榮的城市，將是那些能給人們「就業以外」相聚理由的城市。

paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。那是我人生中最快樂的時光之一。希望有一天我能再訪東京。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited San Francisco with my sister. We went there by bus. The trip took about 9 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和姊姊一起去了舊金山。我們搭巴士前往，路程大約花了9個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a lovely old street. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local dumplings. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一條可愛的老街。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的餃子，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit San Francisco again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪舊金山。

paragraphs.en: I have a turtle named Coco. Coco is naughty but cute. Everyone in my family loves Coco very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻烏龜，名叫Coco。Coco調皮但可愛。我們全家人都非常愛Coco。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Coco waits for me at the door every day. Sometimes Coco also sleeps on my bed all afternoon. When I do my homework, Coco sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Coco都會每天在門口等我。有時候Coco也會整個下午都睡在我床上。我寫作業時，Coco會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Coco gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Coco帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Doudou sleeps on my bed all afternoon. Sometimes Doudou also watches birds by the window. When I do my homework, Doudou sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Doudou都會整個下午都睡在我床上。有時候Doudou也會在窗邊看小鳥。我寫作業時，Doudou會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Doudou gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Doudou帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.zh: 每天，Coco都會在客廳追球。有時候Coco也會每天在門口等我。我寫作業時，Coco會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Coco gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Coco帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Snowy waits for me at the door every day. Sometimes Snowy also follows me around the house. When I do my homework, Snowy sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Snowy都會每天在門口等我。有時候Snowy也會在家裡跟著我到處走。我寫作業時，Snowy會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Snowy gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Snowy帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: I have a hamster named Happy. Happy is naughty but cute. Everyone in my family loves Happy very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻倉鼠，名叫Happy。Happy調皮但可愛。我們全家人都非常愛Happy。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Happy chases the ball in the living room. Sometimes Happy also sleeps on my bed all afternoon. When I do my homework, Happy sits quietly beside me like a little guard.

paragraphs.zh: 每天，Nono都會把我的襪子藏到沙發下。有時候Nono也會在客廳追球。我寫作業時，Nono會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Nono帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to skate. My teacher offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學溜冰。老師主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My teacher smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。老師微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 10 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really skate! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約10週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會溜冰了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: After about 8 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really dance! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約8週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會跳舞了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。老師微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My mother smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。媽媽微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a stormy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是暴風雨的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my brother had a great idea: we could clean my room together at home. Later, we also watch old movies. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著哥哥想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家整理房間。後來我們還看老電影。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

title: Why Learning Languages Is Good for You
title_zh: 為什麼學習語言對你有益

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering learning languages. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了學習語言的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep. Second, it builds confidence step by step. Research also suggests that it gives your brain a healthy break from screens.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。其次，它能一步步建立自信。研究也指出，它能讓大腦健康地遠離螢幕休息。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try learning languages for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著學習語言十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了慢跑的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it reduces stress after a long day. Second, it builds confidence step by step. Research also suggests that it teaches you patience and discipline.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能減輕一整天下來的壓力。其次，它能一步步建立自信。研究也指出，它能培養你的耐心與自律。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try jogging for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著慢跑十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Turkey

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Turkey is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，土耳其也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Turkey, tea or coffee is offered to every guest. It is also common that meals are shared and eaten slowly with family. Perhaps most charming of all, music and dancing are part of daily life.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在土耳其，每位客人都會被奉上茶或咖啡。此外，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的也很常見。也許最迷人的是，音樂和舞蹈是日常生活的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，紐西蘭也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in New Zealand, strangers greet each other warmly on the street. It is also common that old festivals are still celebrated in every town. Perhaps most charming of all, music and dancing are part of daily life.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在紐西蘭，陌生人在街上會熱情地打招呼。此外，每個城鎮仍會慶祝古老的節慶也很常見。也許最迷人的是，音樂和舞蹈是日常生活的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: I still remember the morning of my first part-time job. My hands were cold, my heart was racing, and a small voice in my head kept asking, "What if I fail?"
paragraphs.zh: 我仍記得第一次打工那天早上。我的手冰冷，心跳加速，腦中有個小聲音不斷問：「如果失敗了怎麼辦？」

paragraphs.en: Once it began, however, something surprising happened. I was too busy to be afraid. Every small step took all my attention, and the fear quietly stepped aside. I made mistakes, of course - but none of them ended the world.
paragraphs.zh: 然而一旦開始，令人意外的事發生了。我忙得沒有時間害怕。每一個小步驟都佔據了我的注意力，恐懼就悄悄退到一旁。我當然犯了錯——但沒有一個錯讓世界毀滅。

paragraphs.en: Looking back, that part-time job taught me a lesson no book could: courage is not the absence of fear. It is deciding that something matters more than fear.
paragraphs.zh: 回頭看，那次打工教會我書本學不到的一課：勇氣不是沒有恐懼，而是決定有些事比恐懼更重要。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as robotics. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像機器人技術這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks, and it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - rules and laws have not caught up with the change, and the technology is still expensive and imperfect.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作，而且它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——法規尚未跟上變化的腳步，而且這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美。

paragraphs.en: The future of robotics will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 機器人技術的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as virtual reality. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像虛擬實境這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and the technology is still expensive and imperfect.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could help us use resources far more efficiently, and it could make services cheaper and available to far more people. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - privacy and safety questions remain unanswered, and society needs time to build trust in it.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源，而且它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決，而且社會需要時間建立對它的信任。

paragraphs.en: The future of electric vehicles will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 電動車的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: Facing the Challenge of Food Waste

paragraphs.en: Among the many problems modern society faces, food waste stands out because it touches almost everyone, yet no single person can solve it alone. Ignoring it only makes the eventual cost higher.
paragraphs.zh: 在現代社會面臨的眾多問題中，食物浪費格外突出，因為它幾乎影響每一個人，卻沒有任何個人能獨力解決。忽視它只會讓最終的代價更高。

paragraphs.en: Progress is possible, but it requires action on several levels at once. Communities can share resources and ideas instead of working alone. At the same time, each of us can change one small daily habit.
paragraphs.zh: 進展是可能的，但需要多個層面同時行動。社區之間可以共享資源與想法，而不是單打獨鬥。與此同時，我們每個人都可以改變一個小小的日常習慣。

paragraphs.en: History shows that societies can change faster than anyone expects once enough people decide the problem is theirs. Food waste will test whether we make that decision in time.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史證明，一旦有夠多人把問題當成自己的事，社會的改變會比任何人預期的更快。食物浪費將考驗我們能否及時做出這個決定。

paragraphs.en: It is difficult for us to imagine daily life before antibiotics. Yet for most of human history, people lived, worked, and dreamed without it, organizing their world around entirely different limits.

paragraphs.en: When antibiotics arrived, the change was not instant - early versions were clumsy, expensive, and widely doubted. But step by step it reshaped how people spend their time, whom they can reach, and what they believe is possible.

paragraphs.zh: 抗生素的故事為我們今天遇到的每一項新科技留下一課：革命很少會預先宣告。它們以玩具、工具或新奇玩意的姿態出現——然後悄悄變成我們腳下的地基。

title: Should We Keep zoos open?
title_zh: 我們應該繼續開放動物園嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should keep zoos open has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該繼續開放動物園」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it could save money and resources for everyone involved, and it would push society to try new and creative solutions. On the other hand, older systems and habits are difficult to replace quickly, while the change could be hard to enforce fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源，而且它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方。另一方面，舊有的制度與習慣難以快速取代，同時這項改變可能難以公平執行。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should tax sugary drinks has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該對含糖飲料課稅」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it could save money and resources for everyone involved, and it would push society to try new and creative solutions. On the other hand, some fear it solves one problem but creates another, while the change could be hard to enforce fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源，而且它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方。另一方面，有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個，同時這項改變可能難以公平執行。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: I have a parrot named Snowy. Snowy is a little shy. Everyone in my family loves Snowy very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻鸚鵡，名叫Snowy。Snowy有點害羞。我們全家人都非常愛Snowy。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Snowy sleeps on my bed all afternoon. Sometimes Snowy also waits for me at the door every day. When I do my homework, Snowy sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Snowy都會整個下午都睡在我床上。有時候Snowy也會每天在門口等我。我寫作業時，Snowy會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Snowy gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Snowy帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

title: Why Volunteering Is Good for You (14)
title_zh: 為什麼當志工對你有益

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering volunteering. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了當志工的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it costs almost nothing to start. Second, it brings you closer to friends who share the same interest. Research also suggests that it builds confidence step by step.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。其次，它能讓你和志同道合的朋友更親近。研究也指出，它能一步步建立自信。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try volunteering for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著當志工十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Last summer, I visited Dubai with my family. We went there by ferry. The trip took about 5 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年夏天，我和家人一起去了杜拜。我們搭渡輪前往，路程大約花了5個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a historic castle. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local ice cream. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座歷史悠久的城堡。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的冰淇淋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Dubai again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪杜拜。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a windy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是颳風的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my sister had a great idea: we could bake cookies together at home. Later, we also draw pictures. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著姊姊想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家烤餅乾。後來我們還畫畫。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Germany (10)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Germany is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，德國也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Germany, history is protected in beautiful old buildings. It is also common that old festivals are still celebrated in every town. Perhaps most charming of all, people take off their shoes before entering a home.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在德國，歷史被保存在美麗的老建築中。此外，每個城鎮仍會慶祝古老的節慶也很常見。也許最迷人的是，人們進屋前會先脫鞋。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to play chess. My mother offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學下棋。媽媽主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My mother smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。媽媽微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 5 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really play chess! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約5週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會下棋了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

title: Why Learning Languages Is Good for You (17)
title_zh: 為什麼學習語言對你有益

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering learning languages. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了學習語言的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it reduces stress after a long day. Second, it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep. Research also suggests that it teaches you patience and discipline.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能減輕一整天下來的壓力。其次，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。研究也指出，它能培養你的耐心與自律。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try learning languages for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著學習語言十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: Facing the Challenge of Urban Traffic (17)

paragraphs.en: Among the many problems modern society faces, urban traffic stands out because it touches almost everyone, yet no single person can solve it alone. Ignoring it only makes the eventual cost higher.
paragraphs.zh: 在現代社會面臨的眾多問題中，城市交通格外突出，因為它幾乎影響每一個人，卻沒有任何個人能獨力解決。忽視它只會讓最終的代價更高。

paragraphs.en: Progress is possible, but it requires action on several levels at once. Communities can share resources and ideas instead of working alone. At the same time, companies should treat it as a responsibility, not just a cost.
paragraphs.zh: 進展是可能的，但需要多個層面同時行動。社區之間可以共享資源與想法，而不是單打獨鬥。與此同時，企業應把它視為責任，而不只是成本。

paragraphs.en: History shows that societies can change faster than anyone expects once enough people decide the problem is theirs. Urban traffic will test whether we make that decision in time.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史證明，一旦有夠多人把問題當成自己的事，社會的改變會比任何人預期的更快。城市交通將考驗我們能否及時做出這個決定。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as robotics. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像機器人技術這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and early results in hospitals and schools are already promising. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - the technology is still expensive and imperfect, and rules and laws have not caught up with the change.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它在醫院與學校的初步成果已相當令人期待。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美，而且法規尚未跟上變化的腳步。

paragraphs.en: The future of robotics will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 機器人技術的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as online education. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像線上教育這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could help us use resources far more efficiently, and early results in hospitals and schools are already promising. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and rules and laws have not caught up with the change.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源，而且它在醫院與學校的初步成果已相當令人期待。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且法規尚未跟上變化的腳步。

paragraphs.en: The future of online education will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 線上教育的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to take photos. My father offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學攝影。爸爸主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My father smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。爸爸微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 6 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really take photos! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約6週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會攝影了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to play badminton. My best friend offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學打羽球。好朋友主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My best friend smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。好朋友微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 3 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really play badminton! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約3週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會打羽球了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Last october, I visited Vancouver with my brother. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 9 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年十月，我和哥哥一起去了溫哥華。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了9個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a lovely old street. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local hot pot. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一條可愛的老街。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的火鍋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It was one of the happiest times of my life. I hope I can visit Vancouver again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。那是我人生中最快樂的時光之一。希望有一天我能再訪溫哥華。

paragraphs.en: I have a hamster named Cookie. Cookie is quiet and gentle. Everyone in my family loves Cookie very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻倉鼠，名叫Cookie。Cookie安靜又溫柔。我們全家人都非常愛Cookie。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Cookie follows me around the house. Sometimes Cookie also waits for me at the door every day. When I do my homework, Cookie sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Cookie都會在家裡跟著我到處走。有時候Cookie也會每天在門口等我。我寫作業時，Cookie會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Cookie gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Cookie帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

title: Facing the Challenge of Cyber Security (15)

paragraphs.en: Among the many problems modern society faces, cyber security stands out because it touches almost everyone, yet no single person can solve it alone. Ignoring it only makes the eventual cost higher.
paragraphs.zh: 在現代社會面臨的眾多問題中，網路安全格外突出，因為它幾乎影響每一個人，卻沒有任何個人能獨力解決。忽視它只會讓最終的代價更高。

paragraphs.en: Progress is possible, but it requires action on several levels at once. Communities can share resources and ideas instead of working alone. At the same time, companies should treat it as a responsibility, not just a cost.
paragraphs.zh: 進展是可能的，但需要多個層面同時行動。社區之間可以共享資源與想法，而不是單打獨鬥。與此同時，企業應把它視為責任，而不只是成本。

paragraphs.en: History shows that societies can change faster than anyone expects once enough people decide the problem is theirs. Cyber security will test whether we make that decision in time.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史證明，一旦有夠多人把問題當成自己的事，社會的改變會比任何人預期的更快。網路安全將考驗我們能否及時做出這個決定。

paragraphs.en: Last winter, I visited London with my brother. We went there by plane. The trip took about 9 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年冬天，我和哥哥一起去了倫敦。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了9個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a huge park. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local dumplings. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座大公園。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的餃子，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. Just thinking about it still makes me smile. I hope I can visit London again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪倫敦。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited Amsterdam with my classmates. We went there by train. The trip took about 9 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和同學們一起去了阿姆斯特丹。我們搭火車前往，路程大約花了9個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a tall tower. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local bread. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座高塔。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的麵包，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Amsterdam again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪阿姆斯特丹。

title: A Glimpse of Life in India (11)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and India is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，印度也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in India, history is protected in beautiful old buildings. It is also common that tea or coffee is offered to every guest. Perhaps most charming of all, markets open early and are full of fresh local food.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在印度，歷史被保存在美麗的老建築中。此外，每位客人都會被奉上茶或咖啡也很常見。也許最迷人的是，市場很早開門，滿是新鮮的當地食物。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

title: Should We Limit screen time for children? (19)
title_zh: 我們應該限制兒童螢幕時間嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should limit screen time for children has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該限制兒童螢幕時間」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it could save money and resources for everyone involved, and supporters believe it would improve health and happiness over time. On the other hand, some fear it solves one problem but creates another, while critics worry that the costs would fall on those least able to pay.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源，而且支持者認為長期而言它能提升健康與幸福感。另一方面，有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個，同時批評者擔心成本會落在最無力負擔的人身上。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as delivery drones. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像送貨無人機這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could help us use resources far more efficiently, and early results in hospitals and schools are already promising. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - rules and laws have not caught up with the change, and the technology is still expensive and imperfect.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源，而且它在醫院與學校的初步成果已相當令人期待。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——法規尚未跟上變化的腳步，而且這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美。

paragraphs.en: The future of delivery drones will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 送貨無人機的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: Last spring, I visited Prague with my sister. We went there by train. The trip took about 6 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年春天，我和姊姊一起去了布拉格。我們搭火車前往，路程大約花了6個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a big night market. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local grilled meat. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一個大夜市。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的烤肉，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. I will never forget that wonderful trip. I hope I can visit Prague again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。我永遠不會忘記那趟美好的旅程。希望有一天我能再訪布拉格。

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their memory. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的記憶力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: find a partner who wants to improve too. Two: do not be afraid of mistakes - they show you what to fix next. Three: practice a little every single day instead of cramming once a week.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：找一個也想進步的夥伴。第二：別害怕犯錯——錯誤會告訴你下一步該修正什麼。第三：每天練習一點點，而不是一週猛讀一次。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your memory today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的記憶力上，然後相信這個過程。

title: Why Swimming Is Good for You (7)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering swimming. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了游泳的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it brings you closer to friends who share the same interest. Second, it helps you focus better at work or school. Research also suggests that it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能讓你和志同道合的朋友更親近。其次，它能幫助你在工作或課業上更專注。研究也指出，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try swimming for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著游泳十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a stormy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是暴風雨的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my parents had a great idea: we could read comic books together at home. Later, we also play board games. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著父母想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家看漫畫。後來我們還玩桌遊。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a sunny day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是晴朗的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my family had a great idea: we could make hot soup together at home. Later, we also read comic books. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著家人想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家煮熱湯。後來我們還看漫畫。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Greece (8)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Greece is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，希臘也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Greece, tea or coffee is offered to every guest. It is also common that music and dancing are part of daily life. Perhaps most charming of all, meals are shared and eaten slowly with family.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在希臘，每位客人都會被奉上茶或咖啡。此外，音樂和舞蹈是日常生活的一部分也很常見。也許最迷人的是，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

title: How to Improve Your Writing (11)
title_zh: 如何提升你的寫作能力

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their writing. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的寫作能力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: practice a little every single day instead of cramming once a week. Two: reward yourself after finishing a difficult task. Three: find a partner who wants to improve too.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：每天練習一點點，而不是一週猛讀一次。第二：完成困難任務後給自己一點獎勵。第三：找一個也想進步的夥伴。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your writing today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的寫作能力上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to play badminton. My mother offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學打羽球。媽媽主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My mother smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。媽媽微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 8 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really play badminton! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約8週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會打羽球了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as robotics. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像機器人技術這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks, and it could help us use resources far more efficiently. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - the technology is still expensive and imperfect, and privacy and safety questions remain unanswered.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作，而且它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美，而且隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決。

paragraphs.en: The future of robotics will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 機器人技術的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: How to Improve Your Reading Speed (21)
title_zh: 如何提升你的閱讀速度

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their reading speed. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的閱讀速度停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: find a partner who wants to improve too. Two: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come. Three: practice a little every single day instead of cramming once a week.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：找一個也想進步的夥伴。第二：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。第三：每天練習一點點，而不是一週猛讀一次。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your reading speed today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的閱讀速度上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a snowy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是下雪的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my family had a great idea: we could clean my room together at home. Later, we also read comic books. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著家人想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家整理房間。後來我們還看漫畫。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited Hong Kong with my family. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 7 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和家人一起去了香港。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了7個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a huge park. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local seafood. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座大公園。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的海鮮，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. I will never forget that wonderful trip. I hope I can visit Hong Kong again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。我永遠不會忘記那趟美好的旅程。希望有一天我能再訪香港。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a windy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是颳風的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my best friend had a great idea: we could write letters together at home. Later, we also read comic books. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著最好的朋友想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家寫信。後來我們還看漫畫。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to bake bread. My father offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學烤麵包。爸爸主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My father smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。爸爸微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 10 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really bake bread! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約10週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會烤麵包了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a snowy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是下雪的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my classmates had a great idea: we could write letters together at home. Later, we also clean my room. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著同學們想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家寫信。後來我們還整理房間。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

title: Why Volunteering Is Good for You (15)
title_zh: 為什麼當志工對你有益

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering volunteering. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了當志工的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it brings you closer to friends who share the same interest. Second, it reduces stress after a long day. Research also suggests that it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能讓你和志同道合的朋友更親近。其次，它能減輕一整天下來的壓力。研究也指出，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try volunteering for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著當志工十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: I have a turtle named Pudding. Pudding is very clever. Everyone in my family loves Pudding very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻烏龜，名叫Pudding。Pudding非常聰明。我們全家人都非常愛Pudding。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Pudding watches birds by the window. Sometimes Pudding also follows me around the house. When I do my homework, Pudding sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Pudding都會在窗邊看小鳥。有時候Pudding也會在家裡跟著我到處走。我寫作業時，Pudding會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Pudding gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Pudding帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: During the new year holiday, I visited Munich with my parents. We went there by plane. The trip took about 2 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 新年假期期間，我和父母一起去了慕尼黑。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了2個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a historic castle. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local noodles. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座歷史悠久的城堡。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的麵，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. Just thinking about it still makes me smile. I hope I can visit Munich again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪慕尼黑。

title: Why Hiking Is Good for You (10)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering hiking. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了健行的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it helps you focus better at work or school. Second, it teaches you patience and discipline. Research also suggests that it costs almost nothing to start.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能幫助你在工作或課業上更專注。其次，它能培養你的耐心與自律。研究也指出，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try hiking for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著健行十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as 3D printing. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像3D 列印這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: early results in hospitals and schools are already promising, and it could make services cheaper and available to far more people. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - rules and laws have not caught up with the change, and privacy and safety questions remain unanswered.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它在醫院與學校的初步成果已相當令人期待，而且它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——法規尚未跟上變化的腳步，而且隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決。

paragraphs.en: The future of 3D printing will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 3D 列印的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Portugal (7)

paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，葡萄牙也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Portugal, meals are shared and eaten slowly with family. It is also common that people take off their shoes before entering a home. Perhaps most charming of all, markets open early and are full of fresh local food.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在葡萄牙，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的。此外，人們進屋前會先脫鞋也很常見。也許最迷人的是，市場很早開門，滿是新鮮的當地食物。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: Last spring, I visited Dubai with my best friend. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 2 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年春天，我和最好的朋友一起去了杜拜。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了2個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a quiet lake. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local ice cream. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座寧靜的湖。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的冰淇淋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪杜拜。

paragraphs.en: For example, in India, old festivals are still celebrated in every town. It is also common that music and dancing are part of daily life. Perhaps most charming of all, people take off their shoes before entering a home.

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a colorful harbor. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local local snacks. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
