paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to skate. My best friend offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學溜冰。好朋友主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My best friend smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。好朋友微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 6 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really skate! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約6週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會溜冰了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Last october, I visited Venice with my classmates. We went there by plane. The trip took about 5 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年十月，我和同學們一起去了威尼斯。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了5個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a quiet lake. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local ice cream. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座寧靜的湖。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的冰淇淋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. I will never forget that wonderful trip. I hope I can visit Venice again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。我永遠不會忘記那趟美好的旅程。希望有一天我能再訪威尼斯。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as telemedicine. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像遠距醫療這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants, and it could make services cheaper and available to far more people. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - some workers may lose their jobs during the transition, and the technology is still expensive and imperfect.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭，而且它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——部分工作者可能在轉型過程中失業，而且這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美。

paragraphs.en: The future of telemedicine will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 遠距醫療的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Mexico (10)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Mexico is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，墨西哥也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Mexico, strangers greet each other warmly on the street. It is also common that music and dancing are part of daily life. Perhaps most charming of all, old festivals are still celebrated in every town.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在墨西哥，陌生人在街上會熱情地打招呼。此外，音樂和舞蹈是日常生活的一部分也很常見。也許最迷人的是，每個城鎮仍會慶祝古老的節慶。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as smart homes. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像智慧家庭這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: early results in hospitals and schools are already promising, and it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and privacy and safety questions remain unanswered.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它在醫院與學校的初步成果已相當令人期待，而且它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決。

paragraphs.en: The future of smart homes will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 智慧家庭的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to make dumplings. My teacher offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學包餃子。老師主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My teacher smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。老師微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 8 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really make dumplings! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約8週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會包餃子了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: During the new year holiday, I visited Barcelona with my classmates. We went there by ferry. The trip took about 3 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 新年假期期間，我和同學們一起去了巴塞隆納。我們搭渡輪前往，路程大約花了3個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a huge park. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local grilled meat. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座大公園。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的烤肉，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. I will never forget that wonderful trip. I hope I can visit Barcelona again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。我永遠不會忘記那趟美好的旅程。希望有一天我能再訪巴塞隆納。

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their memory. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的記憶力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints. Two: set a small, clear goal before you start each session. Three: do not be afraid of mistakes - they show you what to fix next.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。第二：每次開始前先設定一個小而明確的目標。第三：別害怕犯錯——錯誤會告訴你下一步該修正什麼。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your memory today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的記憶力上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: Last spring, I visited Kyoto with my parents. We went there by bus. The trip took about 5 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年春天，我和父母一起去了京都。我們搭巴士前往，路程大約花了5個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a historic castle. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local hot pot. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座歷史悠久的城堡。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的火鍋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. Just thinking about it still makes me smile. I hope I can visit Kyoto again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪京都。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited Paris with my best friend. We went there by plane. The trip took about 7 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和最好的朋友一起去了巴黎。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了7個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a colorful harbor. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local street food. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一個色彩繽紛的港口。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的街頭小吃，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Paris again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪巴黎。

title: How to Improve Your Time Management (17)
title_zh: 如何提升你的時間管理

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their time management. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的時間管理停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints. Two: review what you learned before going to bed. Three: set a small, clear goal before you start each session.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。第二：睡前複習當天學到的內容。第三：每次開始前先設定一個小而明確的目標。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your time management today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的時間管理上，然後相信這個過程。

title: Should We Learn coding at school? (18)
title_zh: 我們應該在學校學寫程式嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should learn coding at school has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該在學校學寫程式」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, studies in several countries show encouraging early results, and it would push society to try new and creative solutions. On the other hand, the change could be hard to enforce fairly, while critics worry that the costs would fall on those least able to pay.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，數個國家的研究顯示出令人鼓舞的初步結果，而且它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方。另一方面，這項改變可能難以公平執行，同時批評者擔心成本會落在最無力負擔的人身上。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a rainy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是下雨的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my classmates had a great idea: we could watch old movies together at home. Later, we also write letters. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著同學們想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家看老電影。後來我們還寫信。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to dance. My father offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學跳舞。爸爸主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My father smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。爸爸微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 6 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really dance! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約6週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會跳舞了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as artificial intelligence. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像人工智慧這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - rules and laws have not caught up with the change, and society needs time to build trust in it.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——法規尚未跟上變化的腳步，而且社會需要時間建立對它的信任。

paragraphs.en: The future of artificial intelligence will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智慧的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: Why Dancing Is Good for You (13)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering dancing. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了跳舞的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep. Second, it reduces stress after a long day. Research also suggests that it costs almost nothing to start.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。其次，它能減輕一整天下來的壓力。研究也指出，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try dancing for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著跳舞十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a windy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是颳風的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my best friend had a great idea: we could draw pictures together at home. Later, we also play board games. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著最好的朋友想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家畫畫。後來我們還玩桌遊。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: I have a hedgehog named Nini. Nini is a little shy. Everyone in my family loves Nini very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻刺蝟，名叫Nini。Nini有點害羞。我們全家人都非常愛Nini。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Nini waits for me at the door every day. Sometimes Nini also watches birds by the window. When I do my homework, Nini sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Nini都會每天在門口等我。有時候Nini也會在窗邊看小鳥。我寫作業時，Nini會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Nini gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Nini帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

title: Why Hiking Is Good for You (11)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering hiking. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了健行的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it reduces stress after a long day. Second, it builds confidence step by step. Research also suggests that it costs almost nothing to start.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能減輕一整天下來的壓力。其次，它能一步步建立自信。研究也指出，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try hiking for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著健行十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Last summer, I visited Bali with my parents. We went there by plane. The trip took about 7 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年夏天，我和父母一起去了峇里島。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了7個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a historic castle. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local street food. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座歷史悠久的城堡。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的街頭小吃，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. Just thinking about it still makes me smile. I hope I can visit Bali again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪峇里島。

paragraphs.en: I have a parrot named Ball. Ball is a little shy. Everyone in my family loves Ball very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻鸚鵡，名叫Ball。Ball有點害羞。我們全家人都非常愛Ball。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Ball sleeps on my bed all afternoon. Sometimes Ball also follows me around the house. When I do my homework, Ball sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Ball都會整個下午都睡在我床上。有時候Ball也會在家裡跟著我到處走。我寫作業時，Ball會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Ball gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Ball帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to bake bread. My mother offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學烤麵包。媽媽主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My mother smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。媽媽微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 4 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really bake bread! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約4週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會烤麵包了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

title: Why Learning Languages Is Good for You (18)
title_zh: 為什麼學習語言對你有益

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering learning languages. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了學習語言的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it gives your brain a healthy break from screens. Second, it teaches you patience and discipline. Research also suggests that it brings you closer to friends who share the same interest.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能讓大腦健康地遠離螢幕休息。其次，它能培養你的耐心與自律。研究也指出，它能讓你和志同道合的朋友更親近。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try learning languages for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著學習語言十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to ride a bike. My best friend offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學騎腳踏車。好朋友主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My best friend smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。好朋友微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 3 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really ride a bike! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約3週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會騎腳踏車了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Egypt (7)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Egypt is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，埃及也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Egypt, tea or coffee is offered to every guest. It is also common that markets open early and are full of fresh local food. Perhaps most charming of all, meals are shared and eaten slowly with family.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在埃及，每位客人都會被奉上茶或咖啡。此外，市場很早開門，滿是新鮮的當地食物也很常見。也許最迷人的是，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Iceland (6)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Iceland is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，冰島也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Iceland, music and dancing are part of daily life. It is also common that people take off their shoes before entering a home. Perhaps most charming of all, tea or coffee is offered to every guest.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在冰島，音樂和舞蹈是日常生活的一部分。此外，人們進屋前會先脫鞋也很常見。也許最迷人的是，每位客人都會被奉上茶或咖啡。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Brazil (8)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Brazil is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，巴西也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Brazil, meals are shared and eaten slowly with family. It is also common that old festivals are still celebrated in every town. Perhaps most charming of all, people take off their shoes before entering a home.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在巴西，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的。此外，每個城鎮仍會慶祝古老的節慶也很常見。也許最迷人的是，人們進屋前會先脫鞋。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as 3D printing. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像3D 列印這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - some workers may lose their jobs during the transition, and privacy and safety questions remain unanswered.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——部分工作者可能在轉型過程中失業，而且隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決。

paragraphs.en: The future of 3D printing will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 3D 列印的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: Last summer, I visited Singapore with my sister. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 3 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年夏天，我和姊姊一起去了新加坡。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了3個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a beautiful beach. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local street food. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一片美麗的海灘。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的街頭小吃，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Singapore again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪新加坡。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as wearable devices. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像穿戴式裝置這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants, and it could make services cheaper and available to far more people. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - rules and laws have not caught up with the change, and society needs time to build trust in it.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭，而且它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——法規尚未跟上變化的腳步，而且社會需要時間建立對它的信任。

paragraphs.en: The future of wearable devices will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 穿戴式裝置的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: Facing the Challenge of Youth Unemployment (14)

paragraphs.en: Among the many problems modern society faces, youth unemployment stands out because it touches almost everyone, yet no single person can solve it alone. Ignoring it only makes the eventual cost higher.
paragraphs.zh: 在現代社會面臨的眾多問題中，青年失業格外突出，因為它幾乎影響每一個人，卻沒有任何個人能獨力解決。忽視它只會讓最終的代價更高。

paragraphs.en: Progress is possible, but it requires action on several levels at once. Companies should treat it as a responsibility, not just a cost. At the same time, governments can set clearer rules and invest in long-term solutions.
paragraphs.zh: 進展是可能的，但需要多個層面同時行動。企業應把它視為責任，而不只是成本。與此同時，政府可以制定更明確的規範並投資長期解方。

paragraphs.en: History shows that societies can change faster than anyone expects once enough people decide the problem is theirs. Youth unemployment will test whether we make that decision in time.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史證明，一旦有夠多人把問題當成自己的事，社會的改變會比任何人預期的更快。青年失業將考驗我們能否及時做出這個決定。

title: Facing the Challenge of Food Waste (13)

paragraphs.en: Among the many problems modern society faces, food waste stands out because it touches almost everyone, yet no single person can solve it alone. Ignoring it only makes the eventual cost higher.
paragraphs.zh: 在現代社會面臨的眾多問題中，食物浪費格外突出，因為它幾乎影響每一個人，卻沒有任何個人能獨力解決。忽視它只會讓最終的代價更高。

paragraphs.en: Progress is possible, but it requires action on several levels at once. Companies should treat it as a responsibility, not just a cost. At the same time, communities can share resources and ideas instead of working alone.
paragraphs.zh: 進展是可能的，但需要多個層面同時行動。企業應把它視為責任，而不只是成本。與此同時，社區之間可以共享資源與想法，而不是單打獨鬥。

paragraphs.en: History shows that societies can change faster than anyone expects once enough people decide the problem is theirs. Food waste will test whether we make that decision in time.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史證明，一旦有夠多人把問題當成自己的事，社會的改變會比任何人預期的更快。食物浪費將考驗我們能否及時做出這個決定。

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Korea is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，韓國也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

title: How to Improve Your Note-Taking (21)
title_zh: 如何提升你的筆記技巧

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their note-taking. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的筆記技巧停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: review what you learned before going to bed. Two: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints. Three: find a partner who wants to improve too.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：睡前複習當天學到的內容。第二：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。第三：找一個也想進步的夥伴。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your note-taking today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的筆記技巧上，然後相信這個過程。

title: Why Hiking Is Good for You (12)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering hiking. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了健行的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it brings you closer to friends who share the same interest. Second, it costs almost nothing to start. Research also suggests that it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能讓你和志同道合的朋友更親近。其次，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。研究也指出，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try hiking for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著健行十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: Why Volunteering Is Good for You (16)
title_zh: 為什麼當志工對你有益

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try volunteering for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著當志工十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a snowy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是下雪的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my sister had a great idea: we could write letters together at home. Later, we also clean my room. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著姊姊想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家寫信。後來我們還整理房間。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: I have a goldfish named Bobo. Bobo is naughty but cute. Everyone in my family loves Bobo very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻金魚，名叫Bobo。Bobo調皮但可愛。我們全家人都非常愛Bobo。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Bobo hides my socks under the sofa. Sometimes Bobo also watches birds by the window. When I do my homework, Bobo sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Bobo都會把我的襪子藏到沙發下。有時候Bobo也會在窗邊看小鳥。我寫作業時，Bobo會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Bobo gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Bobo帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - the technology is still expensive and imperfect, and society needs time to build trust in it.

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as telemedicine. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像遠距醫療這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: I have a goldfish named Nini. Nini is very clever. Everyone in my family loves Nini very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻金魚，名叫Nini。Nini非常聰明。我們全家人都非常愛Nini。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Nini watches birds by the window. Sometimes Nini also follows me around the house. When I do my homework, Nini sits quietly beside me like a little guard.

title: How to Improve Your Time Management (18)
title_zh: 如何提升你的時間管理

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their time management. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的時間管理停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: do not be afraid of mistakes - they show you what to fix next. Two: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come. Three: find a partner who wants to improve too.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：別害怕犯錯——錯誤會告訴你下一步該修正什麼。第二：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。第三：找一個也想進步的夥伴。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your time management today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的時間管理上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their memory. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的記憶力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: practice a little every single day instead of cramming once a week. Two: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints. Three: review what you learned before going to bed.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：每天練習一點點，而不是一週猛讀一次。第二：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。第三：睡前複習當天學到的內容。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your memory today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的記憶力上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as wearable devices. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像穿戴式裝置這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants, and it could help us use resources far more efficiently. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and rules and laws have not caught up with the change.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭，而且它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且法規尚未跟上變化的腳步。

paragraphs.en: The future of wearable devices will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 穿戴式裝置的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: Should We Tax sugary drinks? (20)
title_zh: 我們應該對含糖飲料課稅嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should tax sugary drinks has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該對含糖飲料課稅」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it would push society to try new and creative solutions, and it could save money and resources for everyone involved. On the other hand, some fear it solves one problem but creates another, while the change could be hard to enforce fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方，而且它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源。另一方面，有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個，同時這項改變可能難以公平執行。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited New York with my best friend. We went there by plane. The trip took about 9 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和最好的朋友一起去了紐約。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了9個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a tall tower. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local desserts. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座高塔。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的甜點，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. Just thinking about it still makes me smile. I hope I can visit New York again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪紐約。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to make dumplings. My mother offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學包餃子。媽媽主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My mother smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。媽媽微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 8 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really make dumplings! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約8週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會包餃子了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as virtual reality. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像虛擬實境這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and it could help us use resources far more efficiently. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - some workers may lose their jobs during the transition, and society needs time to build trust in it.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——部分工作者可能在轉型過程中失業，而且社會需要時間建立對它的信任。

paragraphs.en: The future of virtual reality will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 虛擬實境的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a sunny day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是晴朗的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my parents had a great idea: we could clean my room together at home. Later, we also draw pictures. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著父母想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家整理房間。後來我們還畫畫。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: I have a turtle named Bobo. Bobo is always hungry. Everyone in my family loves Bobo very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻烏龜，名叫Bobo。Bobo總是肚子餓。我們全家人都非常愛Bobo。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Bobo waits for me at the door every day. Sometimes Bobo also chases the ball in the living room. When I do my homework, Bobo sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Bobo都會每天在門口等我。有時候Bobo也會在客廳追球。我寫作業時，Bobo會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Bobo gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Bobo帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: I have a turtle named Toto. Toto is naughty but cute. Everyone in my family loves Toto very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻烏龜，名叫Toto。Toto調皮但可愛。我們全家人都非常愛Toto。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Toto follows me around the house. Sometimes Toto also hides my socks under the sofa. When I do my homework, Toto sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Toto都會在家裡跟著我到處走。有時候Toto也會把我的襪子藏到沙發下。我寫作業時，Toto會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Last spring, I visited Okinawa with my sister. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 2 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年春天，我和姊姊一起去了沖繩。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了2個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a quiet lake. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local cheese. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座寧靜的湖。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的起司，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Okinawa again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪沖繩。

title: Should We Make museums free? (15)
title_zh: 我們應該博物館免費開放嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should make museums free has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該博物館免費開放」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it could save money and resources for everyone involved, and studies in several countries show encouraging early results. On the other hand, the change could be hard to enforce fairly, while older systems and habits are difficult to replace quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源，而且數個國家的研究顯示出令人鼓舞的初步結果。另一方面，這項改變可能難以公平執行，同時舊有的制度與習慣難以快速取代。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: Last spring, I visited Zurich with my classmates. We went there by plane. The trip took about 8 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年春天，我和同學們一起去了蘇黎世。我們搭飛機前往，路程大約花了8個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a huge park. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local noodles. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座大公園。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的麵，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. Just thinking about it still makes me smile. I hope I can visit Zurich again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。光是回想起來仍讓我微笑。希望有一天我能再訪蘇黎世。

paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該繼續開放動物園」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, studies in several countries show encouraging early results, and it could save money and resources for everyone involved. On the other hand, critics worry that the costs would fall on those least able to pay, while the change could be hard to enforce fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，數個國家的研究顯示出令人鼓舞的初步結果，而且它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源。另一方面，批評者擔心成本會落在最無力負擔的人身上，同時這項改變可能難以公平執行。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: I have a hamster named Nini. Nini is very clever. Everyone in my family loves Nini very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻倉鼠，名叫Nini。Nini非常聰明。我們全家人都非常愛Nini。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Nini hides my socks under the sofa. Sometimes Nini also waits for me at the door every day. When I do my homework, Nini sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Nini都會把我的襪子藏到沙發下。有時候Nini也會每天在門口等我。我寫作業時，Nini會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Nini gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Nini帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as electric vehicles. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像電動車這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and rules and laws have not caught up with the change.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且法規尚未跟上變化的腳步。

paragraphs.en: The future of electric vehicles will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 電動車的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited Barcelona with my family. We went there by ferry. The trip took about 2 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和家人一起去了巴塞隆納。我們搭渡輪前往，路程大約花了2個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a quiet lake. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local ice cream. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座寧靜的湖。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的冰淇淋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Barcelona again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪巴塞隆納。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Morocco (14)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Morocco is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，摩洛哥也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Morocco, meals are shared and eaten slowly with family. It is also common that markets open early and are full of fresh local food. Perhaps most charming of all, history is protected in beautiful old buildings.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在摩洛哥，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的。此外，市場很早開門，滿是新鮮的當地食物也很常見。也許最迷人的是，歷史被保存在美麗的老建築中。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

title: Why Swimming Is Good for You (8)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering swimming. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了游泳的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it costs almost nothing to start. Second, it builds confidence step by step. Research also suggests that it gives your brain a healthy break from screens.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。其次，它能一步步建立自信。研究也指出，它能讓大腦健康地遠離螢幕休息。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try swimming for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著游泳十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Iceland (7)

paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，冰島也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their focus. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的專注力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come. Two: set a small, clear goal before you start each session. Three: review what you learned before going to bed.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。第二：每次開始前先設定一個小而明確的目標。第三：睡前複習當天學到的內容。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your focus today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的專注力上，然後相信這個過程。

title: How to Improve Your Public Speaking (18)
title_zh: 如何提升你的公開演說

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their public speaking. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的公開演說停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: do not be afraid of mistakes - they show you what to fix next. Two: find a partner who wants to improve too. Three: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：別害怕犯錯——錯誤會告訴你下一步該修正什麼。第二：找一個也想進步的夥伴。第三：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your public speaking today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的公開演說上，然後相信這個過程。

title_zh: 我們應該興建更多核電廠嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should build more nuclear plants has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該興建更多核電廠」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, supporters believe it would improve health and happiness over time, and it could save money and resources for everyone involved. On the other hand, the change could be hard to enforce fairly, while some fear it solves one problem but creates another.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，支持者認為長期而言它能提升健康與幸福感，而且它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源。另一方面，這項改變可能難以公平執行，同時有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants, and it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - privacy and safety questions remain unanswered, and some workers may lose their jobs during the transition.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭，而且它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決，而且部分工作者可能在轉型過程中失業。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a cloudy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是多雲的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my brother had a great idea: we could bake cookies together at home. Later, we also watch old movies. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著哥哥想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家烤餅乾。後來我們還看老電影。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

title: Why Yoga Is Good for You (13)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering yoga. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it brings you closer to friends who share the same interest. Second, it helps you focus better at work or school. Research also suggests that it builds confidence step by step.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能讓你和志同道合的朋友更親近。其次，它能幫助你在工作或課業上更專注。研究也指出，它能一步步建立自信。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try yoga for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著瑜伽十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的記憶力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: practice a little every single day instead of cramming once a week. Two: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints. Three: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：每天練習一點點，而不是一週猛讀一次。第二：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。第三：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your memory today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的記憶力上，然後相信這個過程。

title: Should We Allow phones in class? (12)
title_zh: 我們應該允許課堂使用手機嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should allow phones in class has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該允許課堂使用手機」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it would push society to try new and creative solutions, and it could save money and resources for everyone involved. On the other hand, some fear it solves one problem but creates another, while older systems and habits are difficult to replace quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方，而且它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源。另一方面，有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個，同時舊有的制度與習慣難以快速取代。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

title: Should We Make museums free? (16)
title_zh: 我們應該博物館免費開放嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should make museums free has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該博物館免費開放」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it would push society to try new and creative solutions, and studies in several countries show encouraging early results. On the other hand, some fear it solves one problem but creates another, while critics worry that the costs would fall on those least able to pay.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方，而且數個國家的研究顯示出令人鼓舞的初步結果。另一方面，有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個，同時批評者擔心成本會落在最無力負擔的人身上。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as robotics. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像機器人技術這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks, and it could help us use resources far more efficiently. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - rules and laws have not caught up with the change, and the technology is still expensive and imperfect.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作，而且它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——法規尚未跟上變化的腳步，而且這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美。

paragraphs.en: The future of robotics will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 機器人技術的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: How to Improve Your Writing (12)
title_zh: 如何提升你的寫作能力

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their writing. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的寫作能力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: find a partner who wants to improve too. Two: reward yourself after finishing a difficult task. Three: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：找一個也想進步的夥伴。第二：完成困難任務後給自己一點獎勵。第三：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your writing today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的寫作能力上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to draw. My best friend offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學畫畫。好朋友主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My best friend smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。好朋友微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 10 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really draw! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約10週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會畫畫了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as renewable energy. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像再生能源這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it could make services cheaper and available to far more people, and it could help us use resources far more efficiently. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and some workers may lose their jobs during the transition.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用，而且它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且部分工作者可能在轉型過程中失業。

paragraphs.en: The future of renewable energy will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 再生能源的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

paragraphs.en: I have a turtle named Momo. Momo is quiet and gentle. Everyone in my family loves Momo very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻烏龜，名叫Momo。Momo安靜又溫柔。我們全家人都非常愛Momo。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Momo watches birds by the window. Sometimes Momo also waits for me at the door every day. When I do my homework, Momo sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Momo都會在窗邊看小鳥。有時候Momo也會每天在門口等我。我寫作業時，Momo會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Momo gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Momo帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

title: A Glimpse of Life in Germany (11)

paragraphs.en: Every country has its own rhythm of life, and Germany is no exception. Visitors often notice small details that locals no longer see.
paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，德國也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Germany, old festivals are still celebrated in every town. It is also common that strangers greet each other warmly on the street. Perhaps most charming of all, people take off their shoes before entering a home.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在德國，每個城鎮仍會慶祝古老的節慶。此外，陌生人在街上會熱情地打招呼也很常見。也許最迷人的是，人們進屋前會先脫鞋。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

title: Why Reading Is Good for You (12)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering reading. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了閱讀的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it helps you focus better at work or school. Second, it builds confidence step by step. Research also suggests that it teaches you patience and discipline.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能幫助你在工作或課業上更專注。其次，它能一步步建立自信。研究也指出，它能培養你的耐心與自律。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try reading for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著閱讀十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: I have a hamster named Pudding. Pudding is always hungry. Everyone in my family loves Pudding very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻倉鼠，名叫Pudding。Pudding總是肚子餓。我們全家人都非常愛Pudding。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Pudding chases the ball in the living room. Sometimes Pudding also sleeps on my bed all afternoon. When I do my homework, Pudding sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Pudding都會在客廳追球。有時候Pudding也會整個下午都睡在我床上。我寫作業時，Pudding會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Pudding gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Pudding帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their vocabulary. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的單字量停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: turn off your phone for twenty-five minutes and work in short sprints. Two: do not be afraid of mistakes - they show you what to fix next. Three: find a partner who wants to improve too.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：關掉手機二十五分鐘，用短衝刺的方式練習。第二：別害怕犯錯——錯誤會告訴你下一步該修正什麼。第三：找一個也想進步的夥伴。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your vocabulary today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的單字量上，然後相信這個過程。

title: Why Meditation Is Good for You (17)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering meditation. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了冥想的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep. Second, it costs almost nothing to start. Research also suggests that it teaches you patience and discipline.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。其次，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。研究也指出，它能培養你的耐心與自律。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try meditation for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著冥想十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: Facing the Challenge of Water Shortage (13)
title_zh: 面對水資源短缺的挑戰

paragraphs.en: Among the many problems modern society faces, water shortage stands out because it touches almost everyone, yet no single person can solve it alone. Ignoring it only makes the eventual cost higher.
paragraphs.zh: 在現代社會面臨的眾多問題中，水資源短缺格外突出，因為它幾乎影響每一個人，卻沒有任何個人能獨力解決。忽視它只會讓最終的代價更高。

paragraphs.en: Progress is possible, but it requires action on several levels at once. Companies should treat it as a responsibility, not just a cost. At the same time, governments can set clearer rules and invest in long-term solutions.
paragraphs.zh: 進展是可能的，但需要多個層面同時行動。企業應把它視為責任，而不只是成本。與此同時，政府可以制定更明確的規範並投資長期解方。

paragraphs.en: History shows that societies can change faster than anyone expects once enough people decide the problem is theirs. Water shortage will test whether we make that decision in time.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史證明，一旦有夠多人把問題當成自己的事，社會的改變會比任何人預期的更快。水資源短缺將考驗我們能否及時做出這個決定。

title: Why Keeping A Diary Is Good for You (11)
title_zh: 為什麼寫日記對你有益

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering keeping a diary. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了寫日記的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep. Second, it costs almost nothing to start. Research also suggests that it gives your brain a healthy break from screens.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。其次，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。研究也指出，它能讓大腦健康地遠離螢幕休息。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try keeping a diary for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著寫日記十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it reduces stress after a long day. Second, it builds confidence step by step. Research also suggests that it helps you focus better at work or school.

paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著園藝十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: How to Improve Your Time Management (20)
title_zh: 如何提升你的時間管理

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their time management. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的時間管理停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come. Two: reward yourself after finishing a difficult task. Three: review what you learned before going to bed.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。第二：完成困難任務後給自己一點獎勵。第三：睡前複習當天學到的內容。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your time management today, and trust the process.

title: A Glimpse of Life in Italy (8)

paragraphs.zh: 每個國家都有自己的生活節奏，義大利也不例外。旅人常會注意到當地人早已習以為常的小細節。

paragraphs.en: For example, in Italy, history is protected in beautiful old buildings. It is also common that tea or coffee is offered to every guest. Perhaps most charming of all, meals are shared and eaten slowly with family.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說，在義大利，歷史被保存在美麗的老建築中。此外，每位客人都會被奉上茶或咖啡也很常見。也許最迷人的是，餐點是與家人共享、慢慢享用的。

paragraphs.en: Learning about another culture is like holding up a mirror: it shows us that our own "normal" is just one of many ways to live. That may be the greatest gift of travel.
paragraphs.zh: 認識另一種文化就像舉起一面鏡子：它讓我們明白，自己的「日常」只是眾多生活方式之一。這或許就是旅行最大的禮物。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as online education. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像線上教育這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks, and it could make services cheaper and available to far more people. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - privacy and safety questions remain unanswered, and the technology is still expensive and imperfect.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作，而且它可能讓服務更便宜、讓更多人能夠使用。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——隱私與安全的疑慮仍未解決，而且這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美。

paragraphs.en: The future of online education will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 線上教育的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: Why Playing Chess Is Good for You (13)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering playing chess. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了下棋的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it builds confidence step by step. Second, it teaches you patience and discipline. Research also suggests that it helps you focus better at work or school.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，它能一步步建立自信。其次，它能培養你的耐心與自律。研究也指出，它能幫助你在工作或課業上更專注。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try playing chess for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著下棋十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as 3D printing. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像3D 列印這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it may free workers from dangerous or repetitive tasks, and early results in hospitals and schools are already promising. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - the technology is still expensive and imperfect, and some workers may lose their jobs during the transition.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它或許能讓工作者擺脫危險或重複性的工作，而且它在醫院與學校的初步成果已相當令人期待。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——這項技術仍然昂貴且不完美，而且部分工作者可能在轉型過程中失業。

paragraphs.en: The future of 3D printing will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 3D 列印的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。

title: How to Improve Your Public Speaking (19)
title_zh: 如何提升你的公開演說

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their public speaking. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的公開演說停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: reward yourself after finishing a difficult task. Two: practice a little every single day instead of cramming once a week. Three: set a small, clear goal before you start each session.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：完成困難任務後給自己一點獎勵。第二：每天練習一點點，而不是一週猛讀一次。第三：每次開始前先設定一個小而明確的目標。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your public speaking today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的公開演說上，然後相信這個過程。

title: Why Meditation Is Good for You (18)

paragraphs.en: In our busy modern life, many people are rediscovering meditation. It requires no special talent, and almost anyone can begin this week.
paragraphs.zh: 在忙碌的現代生活中，許多人重新發現了冥想的好處。它不需要特殊天分，幾乎任何人本週就能開始。

paragraphs.en: The benefits are greater than most people expect. First, it costs almost nothing to start. Second, it reduces stress after a long day. Research also suggests that it strengthens your heart and improves your sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 它的好處比多數人想像的更多。首先，開始幾乎不需要任何花費。其次，它能減輕一整天下來的壓力。研究也指出，它能強化心臟並改善睡眠。

paragraphs.en: You do not need to be perfect at it - you only need to start. Try meditation for just fifteen minutes tomorrow, and let the habit grow from there.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要做得完美——只需要開始。明天先試著冥想十五分鐘，讓習慣從那裡慢慢成長。

title: Should We Limit screen time for children? (20)
title_zh: 我們應該限制兒童螢幕時間嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should limit screen time for children has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該限制兒童螢幕時間」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, studies in several countries show encouraging early results, and supporters believe it would improve health and happiness over time. On the other hand, critics worry that the costs would fall on those least able to pay, while some fear it solves one problem but creates another.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，數個國家的研究顯示出令人鼓舞的初步結果，而且支持者認為長期而言它能提升健康與幸福感。另一方面，批評者擔心成本會落在最無力負擔的人身上，同時有人擔心它解決了一個問題卻製造了另一個。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

title: How to Improve Your English Listening (18)
title_zh: 如何提升你的英文聽力

paragraphs.en: Many learners feel stuck with their English listening. They work hard but see little progress, and slowly they lose heart. The problem is usually the method, not the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學習者覺得自己的英文聽力停滯不前。他們很努力卻看不到進步，漸漸失去信心。問題通常出在方法，而不是努力。

paragraphs.en: Here are three habits that actually work. One: reward yourself after finishing a difficult task. Two: track your progress in a notebook so you can see how far you have come. Three: review what you learned before going to bed.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三個真正有效的習慣。第一：完成困難任務後給自己一點獎勵。第二：用筆記本記錄進度，讓自己看見成長。第三：睡前複習當天學到的內容。

paragraphs.en: Improvement is rarely dramatic; it arrives quietly, week by week. Choose one habit above, apply it to your English listening today, and trust the process.
paragraphs.zh: 進步很少是戲劇性的；它總是一週一週安靜地到來。從上面選一個習慣，今天就用在你的英文聽力上，然後相信這個過程。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a cloudy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是多雲的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my family had a great idea: we could clean my room together at home. Later, we also watch old movies. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著家人想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家整理房間。後來我們還看老電影。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was a stormy day, so we could not go out as planned. I felt a little sad at first, looking out of the window.
paragraphs.zh: 上週六是暴風雨的一天，我們無法照計畫出門。一開始我望著窗外，覺得有點難過。

paragraphs.en: Then my classmates had a great idea: we could clean my room together at home. Later, we also read comic books. The living room was full of laughter all afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 接著同學們想到一個好主意：我們可以一起在家整理房間。後來我們還看漫畫。整個下午客廳都充滿了笑聲。

paragraphs.en: That day I learned something important: a good day does not depend on the weather. It depends on the people you spend it with.
paragraphs.zh: 那天我學到重要的一課：美好的一天不取決於天氣，而取決於和你共度的人。

paragraphs.en: During the new year holiday, I visited Singapore with my best friend. We went there by train. The trip took about 5 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 新年假期期間，我和最好的朋友一起去了新加坡。我們搭火車前往，路程大約花了5個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a big night market. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local seafood. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一個大夜市。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的海鮮，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. I will never forget that wonderful trip. I hope I can visit Singapore again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。我永遠不會忘記那趟美好的旅程。希望有一天我能再訪新加坡。

title: Should We Work from home permanently? (11)
title_zh: 我們應該永久在家工作嗎？

paragraphs.en: The question of whether we should work from home permanently has moved from casual conversation into serious public debate. Both sides raise points that deserve honest consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 「我們是否應該永久在家工作」這個問題，已從閒聊話題變成嚴肅的公共辯論。正反雙方都提出了值得認真思考的論點。

paragraphs.en: On one hand, it could save money and resources for everyone involved, and it would push society to try new and creative solutions. On the other hand, critics worry that the costs would fall on those least able to pay, while the change could be hard to enforce fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面，它可能為所有相關的人省下金錢與資源，而且它會促使社會嘗試新穎且有創意的解方。另一方面，批評者擔心成本會落在最無力負擔的人身上，同時這項改變可能難以公平執行。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the wisest path is neither blind enthusiasm nor automatic rejection, but small, honest experiments: try the idea at a limited scale, measure the results, and let evidence - not slogans - make the final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 也許最明智的路既不是盲目擁抱，也不是直接否決，而是小規模的誠實實驗：在有限範圍內嘗試、衡量結果，讓證據——而不是口號——做出最終決定。

paragraphs.en: This year, I decided to learn to play badminton. My best friend offered to teach me. At first, I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，我決定要學打羽球。好朋友主動說要教我。一開始我以為很簡單，但我錯了。

paragraphs.en: In the first week, I made many mistakes and almost gave up. My best friend smiled and said, "Everyone starts badly. Just keep practicing." So I practiced a little every day.
paragraphs.zh: 第一週，我犯了很多錯，差點放棄。好朋友微笑著說：「每個人一開始都做不好，繼續練習就對了。」於是我每天練習一點點。

paragraphs.en: After about 10 weeks, something wonderful happened - I could really play badminton! Now I understand: if you practice every day, nothing is impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 大約10週後，美好的事發生了——我真的會打羽球了！現在我明白：只要每天練習，沒有什麼是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I visited Taipei with my family. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 3 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我和家人一起去了台北。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了3個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a lovely old street. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local desserts. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一條可愛的老街。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的甜點，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It taught me how big and interesting the world is. I hope I can visit Taipei again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。它讓我明白世界多麼廣大又有趣。希望有一天我能再訪台北。

paragraphs.en: I have a rabbit named Momo. Momo is naughty but cute. Everyone in my family loves Momo very much.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一隻兔子，名叫Momo。Momo調皮但可愛。我們全家人都非常愛Momo。

paragraphs.en: Every day, Momo waits for me at the door every day. Sometimes Momo also watches birds by the window. When I do my homework, Momo sits quietly beside me like a little guard.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，Momo都會每天在門口等我。有時候Momo也會在窗邊看小鳥。我寫作業時，Momo會像個小守衛一樣安靜地坐在我旁邊。

paragraphs.en: Taking care of a pet is not always easy, but Momo gives me so much happiness. A pet is not just an animal - it is family.
paragraphs.zh: 照顧寵物並不總是容易，但Momo帶給我好多快樂。寵物不只是動物——牠是家人。

paragraphs.en: Last spring, I visited Barcelona with my sister. We went there by high-speed rail. The trip took about 8 hours, but I was too excited to feel tired.
paragraphs.zh: 去年春天，我和姊姊一起去了巴塞隆納。我們搭高鐵前往，路程大約花了8個小時，但我興奮得一點也不覺得累。

paragraphs.en: On the first day, we saw a quiet lake. It was even more beautiful than the photos online. Later, we tried the famous local ice cream. The taste was amazing, and we ordered more.
paragraphs.zh: 第一天，我們參觀了一座寧靜的湖。它比網路上的照片更美。之後我們品嚐了當地著名的冰淇淋，味道好極了，我們又多點了一些。

paragraphs.en: Time passed so quickly. Before we left, we bought some small gifts for our friends. It was one of the happiest times of my life. I hope I can visit Barcelona again someday.
paragraphs.zh: 時間過得好快。離開前，我們買了一些小禮物送給朋友。那是我人生中最快樂的時光之一。希望有一天我能再訪巴塞隆納。

paragraphs.en: Few technologies attract as much attention today as digital currency. Investment is pouring in, headlines alternate between excitement and alarm, and ordinary people wonder how their lives will change.
paragraphs.zh: 當今很少有科技像數位貨幣這樣吸引目光。資金不斷湧入，新聞標題在興奮與警告之間擺盪，一般人則想知道自己的生活將如何改變。

paragraphs.en: The optimistic case is compelling: it opens doors for small companies to compete with giants, and it could help us use resources far more efficiently. Yet the concerns deserve equal attention - society needs time to build trust in it, and rules and laws have not caught up with the change.
paragraphs.zh: 樂觀的理由很有說服力：它讓小公司也有機會與巨頭競爭，而且它可能幫助我們更有效率地使用資源。然而疑慮同樣值得重視——社會需要時間建立對它的信任，而且法規尚未跟上變化的腳步。

paragraphs.en: The future of digital currency will probably be neither utopia nor disaster. Like every powerful tool before it, its impact will depend less on the technology itself than on the wisdom of the people who use it.
paragraphs.zh: 數位貨幣的未來大概既非烏托邦也非災難。如同以往每一項強大的工具，它的影響與其說取決於技術本身，不如說取決於使用它的人是否有智慧。
